text: Why is scattered mutation harder to read than an accumulator loop?
choices: Because the compiler cannot optimize it
Because loops are always clearer than straight-line code
A variable assigned in several distant places has several possible histories at any point
explanation: An accumulator changes many times in one place following one rule, so a single sentence describes it — and that sentence is a loop invariant. A variable assigned in five scattered places has five histories to trace, and two such variables have twenty-five combinations.
